determinacy_enumeration: V1 -- FULLY DETERMINED. Every declaration the fragment depends on -- the protocol, both conforming structures, the sequence and its two elements -- is written inside the measured fragment: A4 = the element's static type is the boxed protocol type `Named` and the call's result is String, both written; A1 = values throughout (structures and Array are value types); A6 = cannot fail (index 0 is valid because the literal supplies two elements, the requirement is not `throws`, and no `try` is written); A8 = the array literal allocates and the two concrete values are wrapped into existential containers; A9 = the call returns normally and cannot suspend. A7 adds no branch under methodology 03 Rule 1.4.7 -- mere variability of the dispatch target across executions is not a branch, and element 0 is written as `A()` here anyway. Witness: the frozen program builds and prints a.

locality_detail.required_for_fact: allocation_copy_move_borrow_destroy and value_vs_storage -- `Swift.Array` is the entity whose contract states that it is a value type with heap-allocated copy-on-write storage, that an array literal creates one, and that its subscript requires a valid index. Its subscript is written inside its own declaration, so it is one hop (methodology 03 Rule 2.2.2). type_and_representation, alternative_value_cases and control_flow_effect need no hop: the protocol, both conformances and both elements are inside the fragment, and Swift's dispatch, erasure and `throws`/`async` rules are specification knowledge (Rule 2.2.3).

hidden_items.checklist_item: H3 -- Overload or dynamic dispatch not locally evident
hidden_items.why: At the local site `let firstTag = items[0].tag()` the body that runs is selected from the element's run-time conformance; `items`'s declaration and its two elements are a DIFFERENT local site of the same fragment, which methodology 04 0.7 excludes from what is local to this one. The candidate set is every type conforming to `Named` -- two in this program, and open to any other module -- so cardinality exceeds 2 and no per-candidate equivalence record under 1.4.0 can be made: A's and B's implementations return different strings from the same call syntax.

`[A(), B()]` bound to `[Named]` wraps each concrete structure in an existential container -- the values gain a type and witness table and change layout -- with no box, cast or conversion token written at the site (The Swift Programming Language (Swift 6.2), docs.swift.org/swift-book, 'Opaque and Boxed Protocol Types > Boxed Protocol Types'). The change is observable through the values' FFI/serialization layout and through the dynamic dispatch it enables. H4 is not the assignment here under the single-assignment precedence: A and B are empty structures, so the container's inline buffer is used and no heap box is allocated in the frozen implementation, and the array literal's own allocation is excluded by H4's container-literal clause. H5 does not trigger (no abnormal exit is reachable: index 0 is valid by the literal written beside it and nothing in the fragment can throw or trap); H1 does not trigger (no implicit numeric conversion exists in Swift); H6 does not trigger (no type in the fragment admits an absent value).
